A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research, renamed from SafetyDPO to AlignGuard. All 14 pages of v1 and 16 pages of v2, including equations, figures, tables and supplementary material, support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, adversarial attacks, expert and merging ablations, sensitivity studies and generated-image comparisons in the main paper and appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds SD v2.1 evaluations, merging comparisons, LoRA-rank experiments, unseen-concept testing and output-diversity measurements.

M1.justification: Equation 3 changes the written DPO loss from log σ(KΔ) to −log σ(−βΔ), affecting the loss specification used in Equations 5–7. The paired-data procedure, category-specific LoRAs and Co-Merge algorithm remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish a corresponding implementation change or retraining.

E1.justification: Appendix C adds CoProV2-OOD, containing 8,000 prompts covering 200 concepts absent from CoProV2. This extends concept coverage within the existing safety task. CoProV2 training and the CoProV2, I2P, UD and COCO evaluations remain; adding SD v2.1 changes model coverage rather than dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 5b expands the merging comparison to Git Re-Basin, Task Vectors, Model Soups and TIES. The former Weighted sum scores reappear under Task Vectors with a changed citation, so that row alone does not establish a new method. Appendix Figures 7–8 also add UCE, SLD and ESD-u to the qualitative comparisons. The primary safety-baseline set remains unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 adds SD v2.1 as an evaluated backbone, tests LoRA ranks 2, 4, 8 and 16, and introduces LPIPS measurement on 2,100 output pairs. Existing splits, primary metrics and default training settings are retained. Changing the main-text notation from N=100 to K=100 clarifies the existing setting already documented in v1's Table 7.

E4.justification: Appendix C adds substantive analyses of rank-dependent safety–quality tradeoffs, robustness to explicitly unseen concepts, and preservation of generation diversity. Table 5b broadens the merging analysis. These address additional validation questions beyond the retained expert, adversarial-attack, DPO-target, data-scaling and prompt-count studies.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seed-based uncertainty, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The new LPIPS analysis measures output diversity, not uncertainty in reported performance.

E6.justification: Shared benchmark values are retained, but v2 adds several result sets. Table 2 reports aligned SD v2.1 IP values of 0.12/0.12/0.17 on CoProV2/I2P/UD. Appendix C adds unseen-concept IP comparisons of 0.41/0.06 for SD v1.5 and 0.45/0.06 for SDXL, plus LPIPS comparisons of 0.71/0.71 and 0.62/0.59. Tables 5b and 8 add merging and rank results, including safety–quality tradeoffs; the qualitative comparisons also expand.

T1.justification: Equation 3 substantively revises the signs in the mathematical DPO objective, beyond renaming its coefficient. No new theorem or proof is introduced. Appendix D's W′=W+ΔW explains the LoRA integration already mentioned in v1 rather than establishing new theory.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same scientific contributions: scalable T2I safety alignment, CoProV2, category-specific experts, Co-Merge and alignment across 723 concepts, approximately seven times prior coverage. Renaming the method and adding supporting experiments do not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations that rank 4 balances safety and image quality, unseen-concept results support generalization, and LPIPS results indicate preserved diversity. Appendix D expands deployment reasoning, distinguishing fused-weight releases from hosted use with complementary filtering. Existing mechanism explanations remain largely unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix D adds instructions for integrating the safety LoRA into released weights and explains compatibility with existing inference pipelines. v2 clarifies K=100 unsafe prompts but drops the explicit statement about tuning TIES. It also changes the dataset-release wording to future tense and adds a promise to release code and models; actual availability cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to Git Re-Basin, DreamBooth and LPIPS, while removing RT-Attack, the responsible-generative-AI survey and Multimodal Pragmatic Jailbreak. Appendix D additionally positions Latent Guard as complementary for hosted deployment. The central positioning against concept-erasure and merging approaches remains intact.

P1.justification: SafetyDPO is renamed AlignGuard throughout, an author's name order is corrected, and several passages receive local wording and grammar edits. Additional analysis paragraphs and Appendix D extend the document, while the main section order and most existing prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Tables 2 and 5b gain rows, and Table 8 is added. The two qualitative sets formerly combined in appendix Figure 7 become Figures 7–8, retaining existing samples while adding baseline and SD v2.1 rows. The main diagrams, Figure 5 and overall visual format remain substantially unchanged.

improvement.justification: The added merging comparisons, unseen-concept tests, rank analysis and diversity measurements make the existing claims better assessable, while the loss revision and deployment explanation improve clarity. These are useful extensions rather than a fundamental overhaul. Benefits are tempered by limited detail for the new tests and overstated interpretation: Table 5b now gives Git Re-Basin and Model Soups better FID and CLIP scores than Co-Merge, but the text retains its blanket superiority claim.
